answer: A network can require each agent to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may claim rewards, then randomly select a beacon committee to audit claims against signed task receipts. A falcon agent that invents identities must fund a separate stake for each one; detected duplicate work is slashed, while honest agents recover their locks. This makes a sybil attack costly in capital and exposes the attacker to losses, rather than letting one operator multiply influence for free across the garden.
